question: Why did the error rate go up on 13 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: A new deployment caused the error rate to spike.
why_chain: Search v5.23 deployment increased error rate.
Increased error rate led to higher error rate for service search in region eu-west.
The deployment occurred hours before the change, indicating it was the cause.

contributing_factors.description: The deployment was not the only change, but it was the most recent.
why_chain: Search v5.23 deployment was the most recent change.
Other changes (like R010) were routine and did not affect the error rate.
The error rate increase was not caused by other changes.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase was due to a new feature or change in the search v5.23 deployment.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase was not accompanied by new features or changes in the search v5.23 deployment.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The error rate increase was due to a change in the catalog service.
ruled_out.reason: The catalog service backup did not cause the error rate increase.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service search in region eu-west rose from 0.48% to 0.92% (+91%), with a change point at 2026-03-13T15:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service search in region eu-west: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.23).
At the same time, request volume for service search in region eu-west stayed about the same (880 per 5 min before, 989 per 5 min after, +12%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service search in region eu-west stayed about the same (141 ms before, 140 ms after, -1%).
Deployed search v5.23 to eu-west (search, eu-west; 226 min before the change; record R009; fit: hours before the change, too early to explain a sudden jump)
Deployed search v2.15 to us-east (routine release) (search, us-east; 94 min before the change; record R010; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
catalog: INFO nightly backup completed (catalog, us-east; 336 min before the change; record R008; fit: describes a symptom, not a change)

reasons: ✗ The closest change event is 226 min before the change, too far to be convincing.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records from the hour before the change
Error logs or traces from the affected segment after the change

actions.action: Roll back the search v5.23 deployment to prevent further error rate increase.
Monitor the search service for any new changes or issues.
Review and test the search v5.23 deployment thoroughly before releasing it.
